key_insight: OpenForgeRL makes it possible to train agent systems that use real-world inference harnesses end-to-end, instead of treating the harness as something only used at deployment time. This closes the gap between powerful multi-turn agent execution and open RL/SFT training stacks.
problem_solved: Modern agent frameworks like Claude Code, Codex, and OpenClaw depend on stateful, multi-process harnesses for reasoning, tool use, and external system access. Existing open SFT/RL infrastructure cannot naturally represent or train these harness-driven workflows end-to-end.
method: Provides an open-source framework for training harness-based agents across diverse environments.
Supports end-to-end training of agents that operate through complex, stateful inference harnesses.
Bridges open RL/SFT pipelines with multi-turn, tool-using agent execution in real environments.
impact: This matters because it gives researchers and practitioners a practical path to train more realistic agents using the same harnesses they rely on for inference. It can improve reproducibility, scalability, and alignment between training and deployment for agentic AI systems.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing SFT/RL training feeding into a harness-based agent loop
Side-by-side comparison of standard training stacks vs. harness-native training
Icons for multi-turn dialogue, tool use, and external system access
Environment map showing agents trained across diverse tasks and systems
paper_title: OpenForgeRL: Train Harness-native Agents in Any Environment
paper_authors: Xiao Yu, Baolin Peng, Ruize Xu, Hao Zou, Qianhui Wu
